elements.title: वर्तमान काल · Present Simple and Continuous
Present Simple and Present Continuous
elements.content_inline:
Present Simple and Present Continuous

Present simple is for habits and facts (आदतें और सामान्य सच):

  • I work in a bank.
  • She drinks tea every morning.
  • Water boils at 100°C.

With he, she, it (or one person's name), add -s or -es to the verb: I work → she works, I go → he goes, I watch → she watches, I have → he has.

Present continuous is for actions happening now or around now (अभी हो रहा है): am / is / are + verb-ing.

  • I am working now.
  • She is cooking.
  • They are watching TV.
हिंदीEnglishTense
मैं रोज़ बस से जाता हूँ।I go by bus every day.present simple
मैं अभी बस से जा रहा हूँ।I am going by bus right now.present continuous

हिंदी का "रहा हूँ / रही है" लगभग अंग्रेज़ी के -ing जैसा है। पर "जाता हूँ" वाला रूप आदत बताता है, इसलिए उसके लिए present simple।

Time words: present simple — every day, usually, always, often, never; present continuous — now, right now, at the moment, these days.

State verbs · स्थिति वाली क्रियाएँ: some verbs describe a state, not an action, and are normally not used with -ing: know, understand, believe, like, love, want, need, have (owning), belong, seem.

✗✓
I am knowing him.I know him.
He is having a car.He has a car.
I am understanding.I understand.
She is wanting tea.She wants tea.

हिंदी में "मैं उसे जानता हूँ" में "जानता हूँ" है, पर अंग्रेज़ी में यह I know him ही होगा। Note: have for eating or activities can take -ing: I am having lunch. ✓ We are having a meeting. ✓ — but not for owning things.

elements.title: Past Simple: Regular and Irregular Verbs
elements.content_inline:
Past Simple: Regular and Irregular Verbs

Use the past simple for finished actions at a finished time (बीते हुए समय में पूरा हुआ काम): yesterday, last week, in 2019, two days ago.

Regular verbs: add -ed.

  • work → worked, play → played, watch → watched
  • ending in e, add only d: live → lived
  • consonant + y → ied: study → studied
  • short verbs often double the last letter: stop → stopped

Saying -ed: it has three sounds — "t" in worked (वर्क्ट), "d" in played (प्लेड), and a full extra syllable "id" only after t or d: wanted (वॉन्टिड), needed. Do not say "work-ed" (वर्क-एड).

Common irregular verbs · अनियमित क्रियाएँ — these must be learned by heart:

Verb → PastहिंदीVerb → Pastहिंदी
go → wentजानाcome → cameआना
eat → ateखानाdrink → drankपीना
see → sawदेखनाtake → tookलेना
give → gaveदेनाbuy → boughtख़रीदना
make → madeबनानाget → gotपाना
have → hadरखना / खानाdo → didकरना
say → saidकहनाwrite → wroteलिखना
read → read (रेड)पढ़नाspeak → spokeबोलना
tell → toldबतानाthink → thoughtसोचना
sleep → sleptसोनाleave → leftछोड़ना / निकलना

The past form is the same for every subject: I went, she went, they went — no -s.

Questions and negatives use did, and after did the verb goes back to its base form:

✗✓
Did you went to the market?Did you go to the market?
I didn't saw him.I didn't see him.

was / were (था / थी / थे): am, is → was; are → were. I was tired. They were at home.

Yesterday I got up at seven. I had breakfast and went to work by bus. In the evening I met my friend, and we watched a film.

elements.title: भविष्य और प्रेज़ेंट परफ़ेक्ट · Future and Present Perfect
Future and Present Perfect
elements.content_inline:
Future and Present Perfect

Future with will: decisions made now, promises, predictions. I will call you tomorrow. (मैं कल तुम्हें फ़ोन करूँगा।) I think it will rain. Negative: I won't (will not) be late.

Future with going to: plans you have already made. I am going to visit my village next month. (मैं अगले महीने गाँव जाने वाला हूँ।) Hindi "जाने वाला हूँ" is close to going to.

Present perfect: have / has + past participle (verb's third form). Use it for a past action whose result matters now, for life experience, and with unfinished time (today, this week). Common words: already, just, yet, ever, never.

  • I have lost my keys. — they are still lost now.
  • She has finished her work.
  • Have you ever been to Goa?
  • I haven't eaten yet.
BasePastPast participle
eatateeaten
gowentgone / been
seesawseen
dodiddone
writewrotewritten
taketooktaken
finishfinishedfinished
buyboughtbought

Present perfect or past simple? The key rule: if you say when it happened (yesterday, last week, in 2020, at 5 o'clock), use the past simple.

✗✓
I have eaten yesterday.I ate yesterday. / I have already eaten.
I have seen him last week.I saw him last week.

हिंदी में "मैंने खाना खा लिया है" और "मैंने कल खाना खाया" दोनों में "खाया" आता है। अंग्रेज़ी में "कल" जैसा समय बताने वाला शब्द हो, तो past simple लगाइए।

for and since (हिंदी में दोनों के लिए "से"): I have lived here for five years. (for + अवधि) I have lived here since 2020. (since + शुरुआत का समय)

TenseFormExample
Present simpleverb / verb-sShe works here.
Present continuousam/is/are + verb-ingShe is working now.
Past simpleverb-ed / irregularShe worked yesterday.
Futurewill + verb / going to + verbShe will work tomorrow.
Present perfecthave/has + past participleShe has worked here since 2021.

elements.title: Capitals and Punctuation
elements.content_inline:
Capitals and Punctuation

Punctuation marks show where a sentence ends and how to read it. Hindi uses the पूर्ण विराम (।); English uses a full stop (.) — a small dot on the line. Never use । in English writing.

MarkNameUseExample
.full stop (US: period)end of a statementI live in Patna.
?question markend of a questionWhere do you live?
!exclamation markstrong feeling; use rarelyWhat a surprise!
,commashort pause, lists, after a greetingI bought rice, dal and sugar.
'apostropheshort forms and belongingdon't, it's, Ravi's bag
" "quotation markssomeone's exact wordsShe said, "I am ready."

Capital letters: the first word of a sentence; the word I; names of people, places, days and months; languages and nationalities (Hindi, English, Indian).

it's or its? it's = it is (It's raining.). its = belonging to it, with no apostrophe (The dog wagged its tail.). Plurals never take an apostrophe: two books, not two book's.

Spaces: no space before . , ? ! and one space after. ✗ Hello ,how are you ? ✓ Hello, how are you? (हिंदी टाइप करते समय कई लोग । से पहले स्पेस देते हैं; अंग्रेज़ी में विराम-चिह्न से पहले स्पेस नहीं।)

  • Don't write whole sentences in CAPITALS — it reads like shouting.
  • Avoid !!! and ??? in work messages.

Practice: correct this — my name is anil i live in jaipur → My name is Anil. I live in Jaipur.

elements.title: मैसेज और ईमेल · Messages and Emails
Writing a Message and a Short Email
elements.content_inline:
Writing a Message and a Short Email

A short email has four parts:

  1. Subject line — short and specific: Leave request for 12 March, not Request or Hi.
  2. Greeting — Dear Mr Verma, (formal), Hello Neha, or Hi Neha, (friendly).
  3. Body — two to four short sentences: why you are writing, the details, and what you need.
  4. Closing — Thank you, or Regards, and your name.

Template 1: asking for leave

Subject: Leave request for 12 March

Dear Mr Verma,

I would like to take one day of leave on Thursday, 12 March, to attend my sister's wedding. I have finished the monthly report, and Sunita has agreed to answer my calls that day.

Please let me know if this is all right.

Thank you,

Rakesh Kumar

Template 2: asking for information

Subject: Question about evening English classes

Hello,

I saw your notice about evening English classes. Could you please tell me the fees and the class timings? I would also like to know if there is a weekend batch.

Thank you,

Pooja Singh

Template 3: a quick message to a colleague

Hi Arjun, the meeting has moved to 3 p.m. Please bring the sales report. Thanks!

Useful polite phrases: Could you please...? · I would like to... · Please let me know... · Thank you for your quick reply. · Sorry for the late reply.

Clear for every reader: phrases like Kindly do the needful, Please revert and Can we prepone the meeting? are common and well understood in Indian offices, but many readers outside India find them unclear. When you write to a wider audience, say exactly what you need:

Instead ofTry
Kindly do the needful.Could you please send the signed form by Friday?
Please revert.Please reply when you can.
Can we prepone the meeting?Can we move the meeting earlier, to 2 p.m.?

ये वाक्य गलत नहीं हैं, बस हर जगह समझे नहीं जाते। साफ़ लिखिए कि आपको क्या चाहिए और कब तक।

elements.title: Common Hindi-Influenced Mistakes
elements.content_inline:
Common Hindi-Influenced Mistakes

These mistakes come from translating Hindi word by word. They are very common and easy to fix once you notice them. (हिंदी से शब्द-दर-शब्द अनुवाद करने से ये गलतियाँ होती हैं।) Indian English is a real, respected variety of English; the aim here is to be understood easily everywhere, in India and abroad.

Instead ofSayWhy
I am having a car.I have a car."have" for owning is not used with -ing
He is knowing English.He knows English.know, like, want, understand rarely take -ing
We discussed about the plan.We discussed the plan. / We talked about the plan."discuss" already includes "about"
Please return back the book.Please return the book."return" already means "give back"
He is my cousin brother.He is my cousin."cousin" covers चचेरा/ममेरा भाई and बहन
I have seen this film yesterday.I saw this film yesterday.finished time → past simple
I am engineer.I am an engineer.jobs need a/an
I came yesterday only.I came just yesterday.Hindi "ही" (कल ही) → just/only before the word
Myself Ravi.I'm Ravi. / My name is Ravi."myself" is not used to introduce yourself
What is your good name?What is your name? / May I know your name?"good name" is a translation of शुभ नाम
Where you are going?Where are you going?questions change the word order

Five-step self-check before you send:

  1. Does every sentence have a subject and a verb, in that order?
  2. Does every single job or thing have a, an, the, my or this before it?
  3. Did you use the past simple with yesterday, last, ago?
  4. Capital letters at the start, full stops at the end?
  5. Read it aloud once. If it sounds like a Hindi sentence in English words, rewrite it.

elements.title: शब्दों पर ज़ोर · Word Stress and the Schwa
Word Stress and the Schwa
elements.content_inline:
Word Stress and the Schwa

In English words with two or more syllables, one syllable is stressed: it is louder, longer and a little higher. Hindi gives syllables more equal weight, so Hindi speakers sometimes stress the wrong part, and listeners may not recognise the word. (हिंदी में सभी हिस्सों पर लगभग बराबर ज़ोर होता है; अंग्रेज़ी में एक हिस्से पर ज़्यादा।)

CAPITALS show the stressed syllable:

WordStressWordStress
photoPHO-tophotographypho-TO-gra-phy
computercom-PU-terhotelho-TEL
developde-VEL-opeconomye-CON-o-my
teacherTEA-chereconomice-co-NOM-ic

Stress can even change the meaning: REcord (a noun: रिकॉर्ड) and reCORD (a verb: रिकॉर्ड करना); PREsent (a gift) and preSENT (to show).

The schwa /ə/ is the most common vowel sound in English. It is a short, relaxed "uh" — very close to the short अ in Hindi, as at the start of अब. The difference: English uses it only in weak, unstressed syllables, whatever the spelling.

WordSounds likeDictionary
bananabuh-NAA-nuh/bəˈnɑːnə/
aboutuh-BOUT/əˈbaʊt/
todaytuh-DAY/təˈdeɪ/
doctorDOK-tuh(r)/ˈdɒktə(r)/

Devanagari cannot show this well: बनाना suggests three equal "आ" sounds, but in English only the middle one is full. (देवनागरी में लिखा उच्चारण यहाँ सिर्फ़ अंदाज़ा है।)

Weak words in sentences: small words like a, the, to, of, and, can are usually weak and quick, while the important words are stressed: I WANT to GO to the MARket. a CUP of TEA sounds like "uh CUP uh TEA".

Practice: clap on the stressed syllable as you say each word. In a dictionary, the mark ˈ comes just before the stressed syllable.

elements.title: Everyday Conversations
elements.content_inline:
Everyday Conversations

Read each dialogue aloud, taking both parts. Then change the names and details and say it again about yourself.

1. Introducing yourself

A: Hi, I'm Neha. Nice to meet you.

B: Nice to meet you too. I'm Sameer.

A: Where are you from, Sameer?

B: I'm from Indore, but I live in Pune now. I work for a software company. What about you?

A: I'm a teacher. I teach maths at a school near here.

Useful: I'm from... · I work as a.../I work for... · I'm studying... · In my free time, I like.... Say I'm Neha, not Myself Neha.

2. Asking for help and directions

A: Excuse me, could you help me? I'm looking for the railway station.

B: Sure. Go straight, then take the second left. It's next to the post office.

A: Is it far?

B: No, it's about five minutes on foot.

A: Thank you so much!

B: You're welcome.

When you don't understand, say so: Sorry, could you say that again, please? · Could you speak a little more slowly? (समझ न आए तो दोबारा पूछना बिल्कुल ठीक है।)

3. A phone call

A: Hello, this is Rakesh from Sharma Traders. May I speak to Ms Iyer, please?

B: Sorry, she's in a meeting. Can I take a message?

A: Yes, please ask her to call me back. My number is 98765 43210.

B: Sure, I'll tell her.

On the phone, say This is Rakesh or Rakesh speaking. Read phone numbers one digit at a time.

4. At a shop

A: How much is this shirt?

B: It's 799 rupees.

A: Do you have it in a bigger size?

B: Yes, here you are.

A: Great, I'll take it.

Polite tone: in English, a direct order such as Give me water. can sound rude even when you don't mean it. Say Could I have some water, please? (हिंदी में "पानी दीजिए" विनम्र है, पर अंग्रेज़ी में "Give me water" रूखा लग सकता है।)

elements.title: ज़ोर से अभ्यास · Practise Out Loud
Practise Out Loud
elements.content_inline:
Practise Out Loud

Speaking is a physical skill: your mouth needs practice, like riding a bicycle. Fifteen minutes every day works better than two hours once a week.

1. Shadowing. Choose one minute of clear English audio that has a transcript (a learners' news programme, a course video, an audiobook). Listen once. Then play it again and speak along with the speaker, a moment behind, copying the rhythm, stress and pauses. Repeat three to five times.

2. Minimal pairs. These word pairs differ in one sound only. Say each pair five times, then ask a partner to point at the word they hear.

PairSoundsTip
vet / wetv – wv: top teeth on lip; w: round lips, no teeth
thin / tinth – ttongue between the teeth for th
then / denth – dvoiced th: tongue between the teeth
ship / sheepshort i – long eelike इ and ई
full / foolshort u – long oolike उ and ऊ
fan / panf – pf: teeth on lip, lips stay open
sip / zips – zz is s with your voice on (ज़)

3. Record and compare.

  1. Read a short paragraph aloud and record it on your phone.
  2. If you can, listen to a model recording of the same text.
  3. Note only two things to improve, for example "I said 'wery' for very" or "I stressed DE-velop".
  4. Record again and listen to the difference. Keep one recording a week to hear your progress.

अपनी आवाज़ सुनना पहले अजीब लगता है — यह बिल्कुल सामान्य है।

4. Find a partner. A classmate, colleague or family member who is also learning. Agree on ten minutes of English only, every day. Easy topics: your day, food, a film, your plans for the weekend. A tutor can also give regular feedback.

5. Fluency before perfection. Don't stop at every mistake. If you forget a word, describe it: "the thing you use to cut vegetables" (knife). Keep the conversation moving.

Next: a read-aloud practice with an on-device pronunciation check, then two speaking tasks. You record yourself and a reviewer sends you feedback.
